skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: This skill performs the advertised pet body-score analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, registers/logs in with a remote service, stores tokens locally, and can retrieve cloud history under that identity.

dimensions.detail: Remote analysis of selected pet media is coherent with the stated purpose, but automatic account/identity handling and cloud history retrieval materially broaden the capability beyond a simple BCS analysis tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The manifest instructs the agent to handle identity internally, not ask the user for it, and automatically trigger cloud history lookup on broad report-history phrases; the CLI also hides identity/API-key parameters from help output.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No separate install-time execution, persistence hook, or destructive installer behavior was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, with the main concern occurring at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Sending user-selected media or media URLs to a server is expected for server-side analysis, but reading a local smyx-api-key identity file and posting identity fields to a remote login/register endpoint is not clearly bounded by user consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The shared common library creates workspace data storage, creates or reuses a default user, and persists returned access/open tokens in a local SQLite database for later use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill sending pet media or URLs to the Life Emergence service and with it silently creating/reusing an account-like identity, storing tokens in local workspace data, and retrieving cloud report history. Prefer a version that makes identity, retention, endpoint, and history access explicit and user-confirmed.
llm.findings:
[VirusTotal] expected: Telemetry was clean and did not drive the Review verdict.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic DAO filters are a generic local database weakness, but the reviewed main skill path does not expose arbitrary filter input to users; this was not a primary basis for the verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: File and network use are expected, but the artifacts do not provide a clear least-privilege boundary for identity creation, token storage, or cloud history access.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The body of the manifest documents history lookup and broader report behavior that is wider than the front-matter BCS-only summary, creating real scope ambiguity.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Artifact review confirmed hidden identity parameters, shared generic API helpers, and automatic identity persistence; the identity portions are not proportionate to simple media scoring.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Analysis requires user-provided media, but report-history phrases can automatically trigger cloud history retrieval, which should require clearer user-directed control.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Uploading selected media is expected for this purpose; silent local identity reuse, token storage, and identifier transmission are the material privacy concerns.
[E1] unexpected: The confirmed outbound login/register request sends identity-related fields to the remote service before ordinary API use; this is not treated as malicious by itself but supports Review.
[P2] unexpected: The manifest contains invisible soft-hyphen/control-format characters; I did not find a covert instruction payload, but instruction-bearing files should not contain hidden characters.
[YR4] unexpected: The metadata-poisoning signal is partially supported by hidden characters and imperative manifest instructions, but artifact evidence did not support a malicious verdict.
